Having bathed at Varadāna, a person obtains the fruit of a thousand cows. / Then one should go to Dvāravatī, disciplined and with regulated food.
Having bathed at Piṇḍāraka, a person gains much gold.
In that holy place, O great king, marks characterized by the sign of a lotus / are seen even today; that is a marvel, O tamer of foes.
Lotuses marked with tridents are seen, O joy of the Kurus; / the presence of Mahādeva is right there, O bull of the Bharatas.
Having reached the confluence of the ocean and the Sindhu, O Bharata, / having bathed with restrained mind in the holy place of the king of waters—
Having satisfied the ancestors, the gods, and the sages, O bull of the Bharatas, / one attains the realm of Varuṇa, blazing with one's own splendor.
Having worshiped the god Śaṅkukarṇeśvara, O Yudhiṣṭhira, / the wise say one obtains tenfold the merit of a horse sacrifice.
Circumambulating clockwise, one should proceed, O bull of the Bharatas, / to the sacred ford renowned throughout the three worlds, O best of the Kurus,
famed by the name of Timī, which grants release from all sins, / where Śakra and the other gods worship Maheśvara.
Bathing there and worshiping Rudra surrounded by the hosts of gods, / a man dispels the sins committed from birth onward.
Timi is praised here by all the gods, O best of men; / bathing there, O best of men, one obtains [the merit of] a horse sacrifice.
Having conquered the son of Diti there, O highly wise one, / Viṣṇu performed purification in ancient times after slaying the thorns of the gods, O king.
Then one should proceed, O knower of dharma, to the praised Vasudhārā; / by merely journeying to it, one indeed obtains [the merit of] a horse sacrifice.
Having bathed there with restrained mind, O best of the Kurus, / and having satisfied the ancestors and the gods, a person is glorified in the world of Viṣṇu.
There is also that supreme sacred ford of the Vasus, O bull of the Bharatas; / having bathed there and drunk the water, one becomes honored by the Vasus.
There is [the ford] renowned as Sindhutama, which destroys all sins; / having bathed there, O best of men, one obtains much gold.
Reaching Brahmatuṅga, pure and with controlled mind, / a virtuous man, free of passion, attains the world of Brahmā.
There is the sacred ford of the maidens and of Śakra, frequented by the perfected ones; / having bathed there, O best of men, one attains the world of Śakra.
Right there is also the sacred ford of Reṇukā, frequented by the gods; / having bathed there, a twice-born becomes spotless like the moon.
Then, having gone to Pañcanada, self-restrained and with restricted diet, / one obtains in order [the fruit of] the five sacrifices as they have been proclaimed.
Then one should go, O knower of dharma, to the excellent place of Bhīmā; / bathing there, a man does not enter a womb again, O best of Bharatas.
He becomes a son of the Goddess, adorned with earrings, O king, / and obtains the great fruit of a hundred thousand cows.
Reaching Girikuñja, renowned throughout the three worlds, / and bowing to the Grandfather, one obtains the reward of a thousand cows.
Then one should go, O knower of dharma, to the excellent sacred ford Vimala, / where even today golden and silver fish are seen.
Bathing there, O best of men, one attains the fruit of the Vājapeya sacrifice; / with soul cleansed of all sins, one goes to the supreme destination.

3.25.m: Nārada said: / Reaching the Vitastā and satisfying the ancestors and gods, / a man obtains the fruit of a Vājapeya sacrifice, O descendant of Bharata.
Right in Kashmir is the dwelling of the nāga Takṣaka, / known by the name of Vitastā, which frees one from all sins.
Bathing there, a man surely obtains the fruit of a Vājapeya; / with his soul purified of all sins, he goes to the highest state.
Then one should go to Malada, renowned throughout the three worlds. / Performing the ritual sipping of water at the evening twilight according to rule,
one should offer sacrificial porridge to the seven-flamed Fire according to one's means, O king. / The wise declare this to be an inexhaustible gift to the ancestors.
Better than a hundred thousand cows, better than a hundred Rājasūya sacrifices, / and better than a thousand horse sacrifices is the sacrificial porridge offered to the seven-flamed Fire.
Returning from there, O king of kings, one should then enter Rudrāspada; / approaching Mahādeva, one obtains the fruit of a horse sacrifice.
Reaching Maṇimant, celibate and concentrated in mind, / having dwelt there for one night, O king, one obtains the fruit of an Agniṣṭoma sacrifice.
Then one should go, O king of kings, to the Devikā, renowned throughout the world, / where the origin of the brahmins is reported [to be], O best of the descendants of Bharata;
the place of the Trident-bearer, which is renowned in the three worlds. / Bathing in the Devikā and worshipping Maheśvara,
making an offering there according to one's means, O best of the descendants of Bharata, / a man obtains the fruit of a sacrifice endowed with the fulfillment of all desires.
There is Rudra's sacred ford called Kāmākhya, esteemed by the divine seers; / bathing there, a man swiftly attains perfection, O descendant of Bharata.
Having gone to Yajana, Yājana, and likewise to Brahmavālaka, / performing the ritual sipping of water at Puṣpanyāsa, one does not grieve over death thereafter.
Half a yojana in breadth and five yojanas in length: / to this extent, they say, extends the holy Devikā, esteemed by the divine seers.
Then one should go, O knower of dharma, in proper order to Dīrghasatra, / where the gods headed by Brahmā, the perfected beings, and the supreme seers
attend an extended sacrificial session, initiated and firm in their vows. / Merely by going to Dīrghasatra, O king of kings, O subduer of foes,
a human being obtains the fruit of both a Rājasūya and a horse sacrifice. / Then one should go to Vināśana, restrained and of restrained diet,
where the disappearing Sarasvatī flows invisibly on the back of Meru, / and is seen at Camasodbheda, at Śivodbheda, and at Nāgodbheda.
Bathing at Camasodbheda, one obtains the fruit of an Agniṣṭoma sacrifice; / bathing at Śivodbheda, a man obtains the fruit of [gifting] a thousand cows;
bathing at Nāgodbheda, a man attains the world of the nāgas. / And reaching the rare sacred ford Śaśayāna, O king of kings,
where the Puṣkaras are disguised in the form of hares, O descendant of Bharata, / in the Sarasvatī, O highly fortunate one, year after year,
they always bathe, O best of the descendants of Bharata, at the arrival of the full-moon day of Kārttika; / bathing there, O tiger among men, one shines forever like Śiva,
and obtains the fruit of [gifting] a thousand cows, O best of the descendants of Bharata. / Reaching Kumārakoṭi, restrained, O delight of the Kurus,
one should perform ritual ablutions there, intent upon the worship of ancestors and gods; / one obtains [the merit of gifting] ten thousand cows and delivers one's family.
Then, O knower of dharma, one should go concentrated in mind to Rudrakoṭi, / where of old, O great king, ten million seers gathered,
overcome with yearnings through their desire to behold the god: / 'I shall see the Bull-bannered one first! I first!'
Thus the seers set out indeed, O king, O descendant of Bharata; / then, having resorted to yoga, O king, by the Lord of Yoga
ten million Rudras were created to pacify the anger of those seers of purified soul, / and stood before the seers.
'Hara was seen first by me,' each of them thought separately. / Pleased with those seers of fierce splendour,
because of their supreme devotion, O king, Mahādeva granted them a boon: / 'From this day forward there will be an increase of dharma for you.'
Bathing there at Rudrakoṭi, O tiger among men, a pure man / obtains [the fruit of] a horse sacrifice and delivers his family.
Then one should go, O king of kings, to the world-renowned confluence / on the most holy Sarasvatī, and worship Janārdana,
where the gods headed by Brahmā, the seers, perfected beings, and cāraṇas / gather, O king of kings, on the fourteenth day of the bright half of Caitra.
Bathing there, O tiger among men, one obtains much gold; / with his soul purified of all sins, he goes to the world of Śiva.
Where the sacrificial sessions of the seers were completed, O lord of men, / reaching that conclusion there, one obtains the fruit of [gifting] a thousand cows.

3.26.m: Nārada said: / Then one should go, O king of kings, to the celebrated Kurukṣetra; / all living beings who go there are freed from sins.
'I shall go to Kurukṣetra; I will dwell in Kurukṣetra'— / he who speaks thus continually is freed from all sins.
There the steadfast one should dwell for a month on the Sarasvatī, O ruler of men, / where the gods headed by Brahmā, where the divine seers and cāraṇas,
the gandharvas, apsarases, yakṣas, and pannagas, O king, / go to that most holy field of Brahmā, O descendant of Bharata.
Even of one who desires Kurukṣetra merely in mind, O Yudhiṣṭhira, / the sins are destroyed, and he goes to the world of Brahmā.
For having gone to Kurukṣetra endowed with faith, O best of the Kurus, / a human being obtains the fruit of both a Vājapeya and a horse sacrifice.
Then, O king, [one should go to] the door-keeper Mattarṇaka of great power; / merely having greeted him, one obtains the fruit of [gifting] a thousand cows.
Then one should go, O knower of dharma, to the unsurpassable abode of Viṣṇu, / called Satata, O king of kings, where Hari is present.
Bathing there and seeing Hari, the source of the three worlds, / one obtains [the fruit of] a horse sacrifice and goes to the world of Viṣṇu.
Then one should go to Pāriplava, the sacred ford renowned throughout the three worlds; / a human being obtains the fruit of an Agniṣṭoma and an Atirātra sacrifice.
Reaching the sacred ford Pṛthivī, one obtains the fruit of [gifting] a thousand cows. / Then having gone to Śālvikinī, the pilgrim, O lord of men,
bathing at Daśāśvamedhika, obtains that very fruit [of ten horse sacrifices]. / Reaching Sarpanīvi, the supreme sacred ford of the nāgas,
one obtains [the fruit of] an Agniṣṭoma and goes to the world of the nāgas. / Then one should go, O knower of dharma, to the gatekeeper [A]tarṇaka;
having dwelt there for one night, one obtains the fruit of [gifting] a thousand cows. / Then having gone to Pañcanada, restrained and of restrained diet,
performing the ritual sipping of water at Koṭitīrtha, one obtains the fruit of a horse sacrifice; / visiting Aśvinītīrtha, one is born handsome.
Then one should go, O knower of dharma, to the supreme sacred ford Vārāha, / where of old Viṣṇu stood in the form of a boar.
Staying there, O tiger among men, one obtains the fruit of an Agniṣṭoma sacrifice. / Then at Jayinī, O king of kings, one should enter Somatīrtha;
bathing, a human being obtains the fruit of a Rājasūya sacrifice. / Bathing at Ekahaṃsa, a man obtains the fruit of [gifting] a thousand cows.
Reaching Kṛtaśauca, the pilgrim, O best of the Kurus, / obtains [the fruit of] a Puṇḍarīka sacrifice and becomes purified.
Then [he should go] to the banyan called Muñjavaṭa, sacred to wise Mahādeva; / having stayed there for one night, he attains leadership among the Gaṇas.
And right there, O great king, [lies] Jayā, renowned in the world; / having bathed and approached it, O king of kings, he obtains every desire.
That is known as the gate of Kurukṣetra, O bull of the Bharatas; / having circumambulated it clockwise, the pilgrim, composed,
at the remembered [tīrtha] of the Puṣkaras, having bathed and worshipped the ancestors and deities / summoned by the great-souled Rāma Jāmadagnya,
becomes one who has accomplished his purpose, O king, and obtains [the fruit of] a horse sacrifice. / Then the pilgrim should go to Rāmahrada, O lord of men,

where, O king of kings, by Rāma of radiant splendor, / having vigorously wiped out the kṣatriyas by prowess, five lakes were frequented, / having filled them with blood, O tiger among men—so we have heard.
All the ancestors were gratified [there], and likewise the great-grandfathers. / Then his ancestors, pleased, said to Rāma, O lord of the earth:
“Rāma, Rāma of great fortune, O Bhārgava, we are pleased with you, / by this devotion to your ancestors and by your valor, O sinless one.
Choose a boon, hail to you! What do you wish, O noble-minded one?” / Thus addressed, O king of kings, Rāma, foremost of eloquent speakers,
with folded hands spoke words to the ancestors standing in the sky: / “If you are pleased with me, if I am worthy of grace,
by the grace of my ancestors I desire the replenishment of my ascetic power once more, / and since, overcome by rage, the kṣatriyas were destroyed by me,
may I also be freed from that sin by your splendor, / and may my lakes become renowned tīrthas in the world.”
Having heard these auspicious words of Rāma, the ancestors then, / supremely pleased and filled with satisfaction, replied to Rāma:
“May your ascetic power increase further, especially through devotion to your ancestors! / And since, overcome by rage, the kṣatriyas were destroyed by you,
you are freed from that sin; they were slain by their own karma. / And your lakes will achieve the state of tīrthas, without doubt.
Whoever, having bathed in these lakes, will gratify the ancestors, / to him his ancestors, truly pleased, will grant what is hard to obtain in the world:

the desired wish of his mind and the eternal heavenly realm.” / Having thus granted the boon, O king, the ancestors of Rāma then, / having bidden farewell to the Bhārgava, pleased, vanished right there.
Thus the lakes of Rāma, belonging to the great-souled Bhārgava, are holy; / having bathed in the lakes of Rāma, chaste and of virtuous vows,
and having worshipped Rāma, O king of kings, one obtains abundant gold. / Reaching Vaṃśamūla, the pilgrim, O scion of the Kurus,
redeems his own lineage, O king, by merely bathing at Vaṃśamūlaka. / Having reached the tīrtha Kāyaśodhana, O best of the Bharatas,
having bathed therein, he attains purification of the body, without doubt; / with purified body, he goes to the auspicious, unsurpassed worlds.
Then, O king of kings, he should go to the tīrtha difficult to attain in the three worlds, / where the worlds were formerly lifted up by all-powerful Viṣṇu.
Having reached the tīrtha Lokoddhāra, renowned in the three worlds, / and having bathed in that excellent tīrtha, O king, he redeems his own people.
And reaching Śrītīrtha, he obtains supreme prosperity. / Having reached Kapilātīrtha, chaste and concentrated in mind,
having bathed there and worshipped the gods and the ancestors as well, / a man obtains the fruit of a thousand tawny cows.
Having reached Sūryatīrtha and bathed with restrained mind, / having worshipped the ancestors and gods, dedicated to fasting,
he obtains [the fruit of] an agniṣṭoma sacrifice and goes to the world of the sun. / Having reached Gavāmbhavana in proper order, the pilgrim,
performing ablutions there, obtains the fruit of a thousand cows. / Reaching the tīrtha of the Gaṅgā, the pilgrim, O lord of men,
bathing at the tīrtha of the Kavyā, a man obtains supreme vigor. / Then, O king of kings, he should go to the door-keeper Lavarṇaka;
at his tīrtha on the Sarasvatī, as that of great-souled Indra, / a man who bathes there, O king, obtains the fruit of an agniṣṭoma.
Then, O knower of dharma, he should go to Brahmāvarta, O lord of men; / having bathed at Brahmāvarta, a man reaches the world of Brahmā.
Then, O knower of dharma, he should go to the unsurpassed Sutīrthaka, / where the ancestors are always present along with the deities.
He should perform ablutions there, devoted to worshipping the ancestors and gods; / he obtains [the fruit of] a horse sacrifice and goes to the world of the ancestors.
Then, O knower of dharma, having reached the other tīrtha in proper order, / having bathed at the tīrthas of Kāśīśvara, O best of the Bharatas,
freed from all afflictions, he is exalted in the world of Brahmā. / And right there is Mātṛtīrtha, where, for one who has bathed, O king,
offspring increases, O king, and he attains the heavenly realm. / Then he should go to Śītavana, self-restrained and eating moderately.
There is a great tīrtha there, O great king, hard to find anywhere else; / it purifies one simply by sight with a single staff, O lord of men.
Shaving his hair there, he becomes purified, O Bhārata. / Another excellent tīrtha there is remembered as destroying the distress of those who bathe.
There, O tiger among men, learned brāhmaṇas intent upon it, / having bathed, attain the supreme state, O best of the Bharatas.
At the tīrtha Svarṇalomāpanayana, O best of the Bharatas, / through breath controls the best of the twice-born remove their body hairs;
and, purified in self, O king of kings, they go to the supreme state. / And at Daśāśvamedhika, in that tīrtha, O lord of the earth,
having bathed there, O tiger among men, they go to the supreme state. / Then, O king of kings, he should go to Mānuṣa, renowned in the world,
where black deer, O king, pierced by the arrows of a hunter, / having plunged into that lake, attained human form.
A man who has bathed in that tīrtha, chaste and concentrated in mind, / his self purified of all sins, is exalted in the heavenly realm.
One krośa to the east of Mānuṣa, O lord of the earth, / is the river known by the name Āpagā, frequented by Siddhas.
Whatever man there offers wild-rice food, / dedicating it to the gods and ancestors, his reward of dharma is great.
When one brāhmaṇa is fed, ten million are [as good as] fed. / Having bathed there and having worshipped the deities and the ancestors,
having stayed for one night, he obtains the fruit of an agniṣṭoma. / Then, O knower of dharma, he should go to the excellent place of Brahmā,
renowned in the world as Brahmānusvara, O Bhārata. / For one who has bathed there in the pools of the seven sages, O bull of the Bharatas,
and at the Kedāra of the great-souled Kapila, O king of kings, / having then approached Brahmā, pure and with controlled mind,
his self purified of all sins, he attains the world of Brahmā. / Having reached the Kedāra of Kapiṣṭhala, very difficult to attain,
having burned away his sins through ascetic power, he attains invisibility. / Then, O king of kings, he should go to Sarvaka, renowned in the world;

having approached the bull-bannered [Śiva] on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight, / he indeed obtains all desires and goes to the heavenly realm, / the foremost among thirty million tīrthas, O delight of the Kurus.
And Rudrakoṭī likewise in a well, and Samantaka among the lakes, / and right there is the tīrtha Ilāspada, O best of Bharatas.
Having bathed there and worshipped the gods and ancestors, / one incurs no misfortune and obtains [the fruit of] a Vājapeya sacrifice.
Bathing at Kiṃdāna and at Kiṃjapa, O ruler of the earth, / a person attains an immeasurable gift and sacrifice likewise; / and sipping water at Kalaśī, faithful and with senses controlled,
a mortal obtains the fruit of an Agniṣṭoma sacrifice. / But to the east of Saraka is the noble Nārada's
auspicious tīrtha, famous as Rāmajanma, O best of Kurus. / Bathing at that tīrtha and casting off one's life-breaths, O descendant of Bharata,
authorized by Nārada, one attains difficult-to-reach worlds. / On the tenth day of the bright fortnight, one should enter Puṇḍarīka.
Bathing there, O king, a person obtains the fruit of a Puṇḍarīka sacrifice. / From there one should go to Triviṣṭapa, famous in the three worlds.
There is the holy river Vaitaraṇī, releaser from sin. / Having bathed there and worshipped the trident-bearer who has the bull as his banner,
with soul purified of all sins, one would go to the supreme state. / From there, O king of kings, one should go to the excellent Phalakīvana.
There the gods, taking refuge in Phalakīvana, O king, / perform vast austerities for many thousands of years.
Bathing in Dṛṣatpāna and pleasing the deities with water offerings, / a mortal obtains the fruit of an Agniṣṭoma and an Atirātra.
And bathing at the tīrtha of All Gods, O best of Bharatas, / a mortal obtains the fruit of a thousand cows, O king of kings.
Bathing at Pāṇikhyāta and pleasing the deities with water offerings, / a person obtains [the fruit of] a Rājasūya sacrifice and goes to the world of the seers.
From there one should go to Miśraka, renowned throughout the world, O knower of dharma. / There, O king of kings, the tīrthas were mixed together by the noble
Vyāsa for the sake of the twice-born, so we have heard, O tiger among kings; / whoever bathes at Miśraka bathes in all the tīrthas.
From there one should go to Vyāsavana, restrained and with controlled food. / Bathing at Manojava, a person obtains the fruit of a thousand cows.
And going to Madhuvanī, the abode of the goddess, a pure person, / having bathed there, pure and restrained, should worship the gods and ancestors.
Permitted by the goddess, he obtains the fruit of a thousand cows. / But he who, O descendant of Bharata, at the confluence of the Kauśikī and Dṛṣadvatī,
bathes with food restricted, is freed from all sins. / From there is [the place] named Vyāsasthalī, where by wise Vyāsa,
tormented by grief for his son, a resolve was made to give up his body, / and he was raised up again by the gods, O king of kings.
Approaching this place, one obtains the fruit of a thousand cows. / Having approached the well Ṛṇānta and given a prastha measure of sesame,
one freed from debts goes to supreme perfection, O lord of men. / Bathing at Vedītīrtha, a person obtains the fruit of a thousand cows.
Ahas and Sudina are two tīrthas difficult to reach, O king; / bathing in both of them, an excellent person would attain the world of the sun.
From there one should go to Mṛgadhūma, famous in the three worlds. / Bathing there at Rudrapada and worshipping
the noble trident-bearer, a mortal obtains the fruit of a horse sacrifice. / Bathing at Koṭitīrtha, a person obtains the fruit of a thousand cows.
Then, having gone to Vāmanaka, famous in the three worlds, / bathing there at Viṣṇupada and worshipping Vāmana,
with soul purified of all sins, one would attain the world of Viṣṇu. / Bathing at Kulampuṇa, a person purifies his own family.
Having gone to Pavana's pool, the excellent tīrtha of the Maruts, / and bathing there, O tiger among men, one is glorified in the world of Vāyu.
Bathing in the pool of the immortals and worshipping the lord of the immortals, / one is glorified in the heavenly world by the power of the immortals.
Bathing according to rule at Śālisūrya of Śālihotra, O king of kings, / an excellent person obtains the fruit of a thousand cows.
And Śrīkuñja on the Sarasvatī is a tīrtha, O best of Bharatas; / bathing there, O king, a person obtains the fruit of an Agniṣṭoma sacrifice.
From there, reaching the very rare Naimiṣikuñja— / for the seers rich in ascetic power dwelling in Naimiṣa, O king of kings,
having undertaken a pilgrimage to tīrthas, came to Kurukṣetra of old; / then the bower on the Sarasvatī was made, O best of Bharatas,
so that there would be a spacious, very pleasing place for the seers. / Bathing in that bower, a person obtains the fruit of a thousand cows.
